reconstructed_theorem_text: Let E be any complete real inner-product space, with its normed additive commutative group structure, and let f:E→ℝ be continuously Fréchet differentiable. Let α, β, ε be real numbers with α>0, β>0, and ε>0. Assume that f is α-strongly convex on all of E, in the precise convention f((1−t)x+ty)≤(1−t)f(x)+tf(y)−(α/2)t(1−t)‖x−y‖² for every x,y∈E and t∈[0,1]. Assume also the global quadratic upper bound f(y)≤f(x)+⟨∇f(x),y−x⟩+(β/2)‖y−x‖² for every x,y∈E, where ∇f(x) is the Riesz representative of the Fréchet derivative. For every global minimizer x⋆∈E (meaning f(x⋆)≤f(x) for all x∈E), every initial point x₀∈E, and every natural number N including zero, suppose the conditional iteration bound holds: if ‖x₀−x⋆‖>0, then 2(β/α)log(‖x₀−x⋆‖/ε)≤N, with N regarded as a real number. Define xₖ₊₁=xₖ−β⁻¹∇f(xₖ), starting at x₀. Then ‖x_N−x⋆‖≤ε. The logarithm is the real natural logarithm, with Lean's totalized convention log(0)=0. The iteration hypothesis imposes no restriction on N when x₀=x⋆. Zero iterations returns x₀. No finite-dimensionality or separate relation α≤β is assumed.
objects: E, f, α, β, ε, x⋆, x₀, N, ∇f and the N-fold gradient-descent iterate
domains: E is an arbitrary complete real inner-product space; f:E→ℝ; α,β,ε∈ℝ; x⋆,x₀∈E; N∈ℕ.
quantifiers: Universally quantified E and structures, f, α, β, ε, followed by the stated assumptions; every global minimizer x⋆, every x₀ and every N satisfying the conditional iteration bound. The quadratic upper bound is for every ordered pair x,y∈E.
assumptions: C¹ regularity; global α-strong convexity with α/2 normalization; α>0, β>0, ε>0; global quadratic upper model with β/2 normalization and the gradient inner-product term; x⋆ is a global minimizer; positivity of initial distance implies the explicit logarithmic lower bound on N.
conclusion: The norm distance between the N-fold iterate of x↦x−β⁻¹•gradient(f,x) applied to x₀ and x⋆ is at most ε.
scopes: All analytic assumptions and minimization are global on E. Existence of a minimizer is not concluded: x⋆ is supplied under the minimizer hypothesis.
constant_dependencies: The sufficient iteration threshold is exactly 2(β/α)log(‖x₀−x⋆‖/ε), and the step is exactly β⁻¹. There is no hidden dimension factor or unspecified constant.
observations: When x₀=x⋆, the iteration condition is vacuous and the result holds for all natural N.
When 0<‖x₀−x⋆‖≤ε, the logarithmic threshold is nonpositive, so every natural N meets it.
When N=0 and the initial distance is positive, the threshold condition forces the initial distance to be at most ε.
The statement gives a sufficient bound on N and an absolute distance guarantee, without asserting necessity, an integer ceiling formula, or an objective-gap bound.
